title: Slab 5 %: current-year equity STCL of Rs 20,000 with slab STCG of Rs 20,000 and equity LTCG of Rs 2.25 lakh: STCL absorbs the LTCG
rules: Income-tax Act 1961 s.50AA: gain on units of a specified (debt) mutual fund acquired on/after 1-Apr-2023 is deemed short-term capital gain, taxed at the slab rate

Income-tax Act 1961 s.70 (Income-tax Act 2025 s.108 [secondary mapping, not verified]): s.70(2) a short-term capital loss may be set off against any other capital gain, short-term or long-term, of the same year; s.70(3) a long-term capital loss only against long-term capital gain
Income-tax Act 1961 s.111A(1) as amended by Finance (No.2) Act 2024: STCG on STT-paid equity 20 % for transfers on/after 23-Jul-2024

Income-tax Act 1961 s.112A(1) as amended by Finance (No.2) Act 2024: 12.5 % on long-term capital gains 'exceeding one lakh twenty-five thousand rupees' for transfers on/after 23-Jul-2024; the gains are those included in total income, i.e. after the s.70 / s.74 set-off
Health and Education Cess 4 % (Finance Act 2025 s.2)
derivation: PINE SHORT DURATION FUND - GROWTH: 10,000 units @ 20.00 bought 2023-06-01, redeemed 2025-09-01 @ 22.00 -> proceeds 2,20,000.00, cost 2,00,000.00, gain 20,000.00; bought after 1-Apr-2023 -> s.50AA deemed short-term at slab (5 %).

s.70(2) lets the STCL absorb any capital gain but does not say which first (interpretive). Reading taken: the assessee may choose and the set-off goes to the gain taxed at the higher rate, here LTCG above the threshold at 12.5 % rather than slab STCG at 5 %.
Tax 11,000.00; cess 440.00; total 11,440.00. Slab is treated as a flat marginal rate; the basic-exemption shortfall and s.87A are ignored, as in every case of this corpus.
Alternative (STCL against the slab STCG first): STCG 0; LTCG 2,25,000 - 1,25,000 = 1,00,000 x 0.125 = 12,500.00; cess 500.00; total 13,000.00; exemption_used 1,25,000.00.
